name: Gods, Pharaohs and the River
description: Three thousand years of Egypt: pyramids, temples and tombs, gods and scribes, from the first farmers on the Nile to the last queen.

checkpoints.name: The gift of the Nile
checkpoints.note: Farmers along the Nile River used its yearly flood to grow grain. Their kings united the land, scribes invented hieroglyphs and wrote on papyrus, a calendar was devised, and the Pyramid of Djoser showed what stone could do.

checkpoints.name: Age of the pyramids
checkpoints.note: At Giza the Great Pyramid and the Sphinx were raised for kings who were thought to become gods, and a boat was buried beside Khufu. Later, after a time of division, a new line of kings reunited the land.

checkpoints.name: Empire and splendour
checkpoints.note: Middle Kingdom kings began the temple of Karnak. In the New Kingdom, Egyptian armies reached far beyond the Nile, Hatshepsut and Thutmose III ruled, Akhenaten promoted the sun disc Aten, kings were buried in the Valley of the Kings with the Book of the Dead, and Ramesses II fought at Kadesh and built Abu Simbel.

checkpoints.name: Kush and the late dynasties
checkpoints.note: Egypt's power shrank. The kingdom of Kush to the south grew strong and even ruled Egypt for a time, and in the end Persian rulers took the Nile land before Alexander the Great arrived.

checkpoints.name: The Ptolemies and Cleopatra
checkpoints.note: Alexander founded Alexandria, and his general's family ruled as the Ptolemaic kingdom. They built the Library and the Lighthouse, put up the Rosetta Stone, and ended with Cleopatra, beaten at Actium by Rome.

checkpoints.name: Rome, silence and decoding
checkpoints.note: After Actium Egypt becomes a Roman province. Its hieroglyphs fall out of use, and the script is read again only after Jean-Francois Champollion works it out from the Rosetta Stone in 1822.
